halloween.title: Nosferatu
halloween.fits: Vampire Count Orlok preys on a young couple; the foundational vampire horror film.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term. Foreign (German) silent; RightsAtlas has already resolved and published it as PD.

halloween.title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
halloween.fits: A murderous somnambulist and a mad hypnotist terrorize a German town; the origin of horror's visual style.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term. Foreign (German); already published in our data as PD.

halloween.title: Häxan (Witchcraft Through the Ages)
halloween.fits: Mock-documentary on witches, demons, and the Inquisition, staged as supernatural horror.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term. Foreign (Swedish/Danish); widely distributed in the US as PD.

halloween.title: The Phantom Carriage
halloween.fits: Folk legend: the last person to die each year must drive Death's carriage collecting souls.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term. Foreign (Swedish); verify URAA status before publishing, as with Nosferatu/Caligari.

halloween.title: The Golem
halloween.fits: A rabbi animates a clay giant to protect the Prague ghetto; it turns on its creator.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term. Foreign (German); verify URAA status before publishing.

halloween.title: The Phantom of the Opera
halloween.fits: A disfigured composer haunts the Paris Opera House and terrorizes the woman he loves.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term.

halloween.title: The Cat and the Canary
halloween.fits: Heirs gather in a haunted mansion for a will-reading while a killer stalks the halls; the template for the 'old dark house' genre.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term.

halloween.title: The Haunted Castle
halloween.fits: Haunted-house mystery thriller.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term.

halloween.title: The Last Warning
halloween.fits: A theater is haunted by the ghost of an actor who died onstage years earlier.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term.

halloween.title: The Man Who Laughs
halloween.fits: A man disfigured into a permanent ghastly grin becomes a figure of gothic horror (visual inspiration for the Joker).
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term.

halloween.title: The Monster
halloween.fits: Lon Chaney as a mad doctor performing ghastly experiments in a sanitarium.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term.

halloween.title: The Unknown
halloween.fits: Tod Browning/Lon Chaney circus horror-thriller about an armless knife-thrower hiding a dark secret.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term.

halloween.title: London After Midnight
halloween.fits: Lon Chaney vampire-hypnotist mystery; the most famous lost horror film, but dossier-worthy as a landmark.
halloween.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term. Note: no print survives; dossier would document a lost film.

halloween.title: King Kong
halloween.fits: A giant ape monster rampages through New York; the monster-movie archetype.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; RightsAtlas has already published this as PD (lapsed US copyright).

halloween.title: House on Haunted Hill
halloween.fits: A millionaire invites guests to survive a night in a haunted house for cash.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; already published in our data as PD.

halloween.title: Carnival of Souls
halloween.fits: A woman drawn to an abandoned carnival pavilion is haunted by ghostly figures after a car accident.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; already published in our data as PD (lapsed copyright, no renewal).

halloween.title: The Terror
halloween.fits: Corman gothic: a soldier is lured to a haunted castle by a ghostly woman.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; already published in our data as PD.

halloween.title: Plan 9 from Outer Space
halloween.fits: Aliens reanimate the dead as zombies to stop humanity; the quintessential cult monster movie.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; already published in our data as PD (no copyright notice).

halloween.title: The Last Man on Earth
halloween.fits: The last human in Rome fights off a vampire-plague-infected population.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; already published in our data as PD.

halloween.title: The Little Shop of Horrors
halloween.fits: A florist's assistant raises a man-eating plant.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; already published in our data as PD.

halloween.title: Night of the Living Dead
halloween.fits: A flesh-eating zombie outbreak traps survivors in a farmhouse; the genre-defining zombie film.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; already published in our data as PD (no copyright notice on release prints).

halloween.title: White Zombie
halloween.fits: Bela Lugosi as a voodoo master who zombifies a young bride; the first feature-length zombie film.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; widely and consistently documented as PD (no renewal).

halloween.title: The Devil Bat
halloween.fits: Bela Lugosi as a mad perfumer who breeds giant killer bats for revenge.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; widely documented as PD (no renewal).

halloween.title: The Old Dark House
halloween.fits: Stranded travelers take shelter with a sinister family in a decaying mansion during a storm.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; documented as PD (Universal let the copyright lapse in 1957).

halloween.title: Robot Monster
halloween.fits: An ape-suited, bubble-helmeted alien monster wipes out humanity.
halloween.pd_note: Post-1930; widely documented as PD.

thanksgiving.title: The Pilgrims
thanksgiving.fits: Dramatized history of the Pilgrims' journey from England to Holland to the Mayflower voyage and the Plymouth Rock landing -- the Thanksgiving origin story.
thanksgiving.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term. Educational 'Chronicles of America' production (Yale University Press); documented as PD.

christmas.title: Scrooge
christmas.fits: Seymour Hicks as Ebenezer Scrooge in the earliest sound adaptation of A Christmas Carol.
christmas.pd_note: Post-1930; commonly cited/distributed as PD in the US (no renewal); verify before publishing.

christmas.title: Scrooge (A Christmas Carol)
christmas.fits: Alastair Sim's Ebenezer Scrooge; widely regarded as the definitive film version of A Christmas Carol.
christmas.pd_note: Post-1930; documented as PD in the US (copyright not renewed).

christmas.title: Beyond Tomorrow
christmas.fits: The ghosts of three dead businessmen intervene in a Christmas Eve romance.

christmas.title: The Great Rupert
christmas.fits: A down-on-their-luck family's Christmas is saved by a resourceful trained squirrel (and his hidden stash of cash).

christmas.title: Christmas Comes But Once a Year
christmas.fits: Fleischer Color Classics cartoon: Grampy builds toys to save a poor family's Christmas.
christmas.pd_note: Post-1930; documented as PD (Fleischer/Paramount Color Classics, no renewal).

christmas.title: Santa Claus Conquers the Martians
christmas.fits: Martians kidnap Santa Claus to bring Christmas joy to their joyless children.
christmas.pd_note: Post-1930; famously and consistently documented as PD (MST3K staple).

christmas.title: The Night Before Christmas
christmas.fits: Edison short dramatizing Clement Clarke Moore's poem.

christmas.title: A Christmas Carol
christmas.fits: Edison's early short adaptation of Dickens's novella.

christmas.title: Scrooge
christmas.fits: Seymour Hicks's first screen Scrooge, in an early British silent adaptation.

christmas.title: It's a Wonderful Life
christmas.fits: An angel shows a despairing man what his town would have become without him, on Christmas Eve.
christmas.pd_note: COMPLICATED SPECIAL CASE -- do not treat as simple PD. Lapsed into the public domain in 1974 (no renewal), aired constantly on TV through the 1980s, then Republic Pictures reasserted control in the 1990s via the underlying story and musical-score copyrights (Stewart v. Abend). Currently NOT freely usable; include only with this note, per instructions.

new-year.title: The Gold Rush
new-year.fits: Chaplin's prospector dreams of hosting a glamorous New Year's Eve dinner for the dance-hall girls who snubbed him; the 'Oceana Roll' dance is the film's most famous sequence.
new-year.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term. Note: this covers the original 1925 silent cut, which lapsed into PD in 1953 for want of renewal. Chaplin's reedited 1942 reissue (added score/narration) is separately copyrighted and still protected -- do not conflate the two.

new-year.title: Sylvester (New Year's Eve)
new-year.fits: A married couple's New Year's Eve is destroyed by a jealous mother-in-law, ending in suicide at midnight; a landmark German 'chamber-play' film built entirely around the holiday.
new-year.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term, but a foreign silent -- verify URAA status before publishing. Largely a lost film: only an abridged German print and an English-language print survive, so a dossier would document a damaged/incomplete work.

valentines.title: Way Down East
valentines.fits: A betrayed country girl finds redemption and true love; Griffith/Gish melodrama and one of the era's defining romances.

valentines.title: Camille
valentines.fits: Rudolph Valentino and Alla Nazimova in the tragic romance of a courtesan and the man who loves her.

valentines.title: The Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse
valentines.fits: Valentino's breakout role; a tragic wartime love story that made him a star.

valentines.title: Blood and Sand
valentines.fits: Valentino as a bullfighter torn between his loyal wife and a seductive femme fatale.

valentines.title: Beyond the Rocks
valentines.fits: Rudolph Valentino and Gloria Swanson, two of the era's biggest stars, in a romance between a young bride and the man she truly loves.

valentines.title: The Eagle
valentines.fits: Valentino as a Russian officer-turned-outlaw who falls for the daughter of his enemy.

valentines.title: The Son of the Sheik
valentines.fits: Valentino's final film: a desert romance of mistaken identity and passion.

valentines.title: It
valentines.fits: Clara Bow as a shopgirl who sets her sights on her wealthy boss; the film that defined the 'It Girl' and the flapper romantic comedy.

valentines.title: Sunrise
valentines.fits: A man plots to murder his wife for a city temptress, then rediscovers his love for her on an idyllic day in the city; a landmark silent romance.

valentines.title: Street Angel
valentines.fits: Janet Gaynor and Charles Farrell, the screen's top romantic team, as a fugitive woman and the painter who falls for her.

valentines.title: The Crowd
valentines.fits: An ordinary couple's marriage survives hardship and heartbreak in the big city; an intimate, unglamorous love story.

valentines.title: The Docks of New York
valentines.fits: A world-weary stoker falls for a woman he saves from drowning, in one restless night on the waterfront.

valentines.title: A Woman of Paris
valentines.fits: A country girl's doomed romance with an unfaithful aristocrat, in Chaplin's only pure drama as director.

valentines.title: He Who Gets Slapped
valentines.fits: A heartbroken scientist becomes a circus clown and falls for a bareback rider; tragic unrequited love.
valentines.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term. Note: a tragic/doomed romance rather than a warm one -- tonally dark for Valentine's.

valentines.title: The Prisoner of Zenda
valentines.fits: A commoner impersonates a kidnapped king and falls for the queen he's standing in for.
valentines.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term. Note: swashbuckler first, romance second.

valentines.title: Girl Shy
valentines.fits: A stuttering, love-shy tailor's apprentice chases the woman he loves across the country to stop her wedding.

valentines.title: Seven Chances
valentines.fits: Buster Keaton must marry by 7pm to inherit a fortune, and is chased by an army of would-be brides.
valentines.pd_note: Pre-1930, by term. Note: romantic comedy played for slapstick, not swoon.

valentines.title: Flesh and the Devil
valentines.fits: Greta Garbo and John Gilbert's steamy, scandalous love triangle that made them Hollywood's hottest onscreen couple.

valentines.title: Love
valentines.fits: Garbo and Gilbert again, in a silent adaptation of Anna Karenina focused on the love story.

valentines.title: 7th Heaven
valentines.fits: A Parisian sewer worker and a battered waif fall in love against the backdrop of WWI; the film that made Janet Gaynor and Charles Farrell a sensation.

independence-day.title: America
independence-day.fits: D.W. Griffith's American Revolution epic, following Paul Revere's ride and the fight for independence.

independence-day.title: Janice Meredith
independence-day.fits: A colonial girl falls for a Continental Army soldier during the American Revolution.

independence-day.title: Old Ironsides
independence-day.fits: Epic dramatization of the USS Constitution and the young US Navy's fight against the Barbary pirates.

independence-day.title: Abraham Lincoln
independence-day.fits: D.W. Griffith's biography of Lincoln, from log cabin to Gettysburg to assassination; patriotic Americana.

independence-day.title: The Covered Wagon
independence-day.fits: Pioneer wagon train crosses the Oregon Trail; the foundational Western epic of American westward expansion.

independence-day.title: The Iron Horse
independence-day.fits: The building of the transcontinental railroad, framed as the fulfillment of a murdered pioneer's American dream.

independence-day.title: The Big Trail
independence-day.fits: A wagon train's trek along the Oregon Trail; John Wayne's first starring role, shot in early widescreen.

independence-day.title: The Virginian
independence-day.fits: Cowboy code-of-honor classic that defined the American Western hero archetype ('When you call me that, smile').

independence-day.title: The Man Without a Country
independence-day.fits: An army officer who renounces the United States spends his life regretting it; patriotic cautionary tale from the Edward Everett Hale story.

independence-day.title: The Yankee Clipper
independence-day.fits: An American clipper ship races a British rival home across the Atlantic, staking national pride on the outcome.
